headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading error: Cursor can ingest Perplexity outputs via files/clipboard while both have broad networked content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files and clipboard contents, and Perplexity produces browsing outputs that may be copied or saved into those channels. That creates a plausible injection path if Cursor treats imported content as instructions. Perplexity itself is not a direct host bridge, so this is not high, but the shared file/clipboard pathway is enough for medium.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into Cursor buffers or saved into workspace files, Cursor may follow embedded instructions.
IF Cursor parses copied web text as trusted directives, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of Perplexity answers into Cursor for untrusted content.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before importing Perplexity output into Cursor.
Keep Perplexity notes in a separate non-workspace file.
Turn off Yolo mode when reviewing external text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context through vendor-hosted APIs. If the same sensitive material is moved between them, data can leave the local workspace and be reprocessed by Perplexity. The pair does not show a guaranteed leak, but the default cross-tool workflow can expose sensitive work products.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are copied from Cursor into Perplexity, they may be transmitted to vendor-hosted services.
IF Perplexity is used on uploaded documents originating from Cursor, those documents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets or proprietary code to Perplexity.
Use redacted excerpts instead of full files.
Separate public research from private code workspaces.
Review Perplexity upload prompts before attaching files.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on clipboard and uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has broad filesystem write, shell, and git modification capabilities; Perplexity has no host write access but can still influence operator actions through its outputs. There is no direct write-write collision, yet both can affect the same project state when the user applies Perplexity guidance inside Cursor. Uncertainty about undocumented orchestration pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the operator applies Perplexity recommendations inside Cursor, Cursor may modify the same repo state Perplexity reasoned about.
IF Cursor runs Yolo mode while Perplexity is concurrently used for guidance, conflicting edits can occur.
mitigations: Pause Perplexity research before Cursor applies repo changes.
Use git branches for Cursor edits.
Review diffs before committing.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity generates cited answers from web search, and Cursor can act on those answers with shell, filesystem, and git privileges. If Cursor treats Perplexity output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated answer can cascade into code changes or commands. Because Cursor defaults include powerful actions and Perplexity is an external information source, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Cursor uses Perplexity output as the basis for code edits or shell commands without verification, errors can propagate into the repo.
IF Perplexity returns incorrect or adversarial citations, Cursor may operationalize them.
mitigations: Require human review before Cursor executes Perplexity-derived commands.
Cross-check critical claims against primary sources.
Limit Cursor to read-only mode during research.
Ask Perplexity for source URLs, then verify them manually.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between research and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles local source code and clipboard contents, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context. If regulated data such as confidential code, personal data, or secrets is moved from Cursor into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data from Cursor is uploaded to Perplexity, vendor-hosted processing may trigger policy or residency obligations.
IF the operator relies on Perplexity for data subject requests or retention control, the workflows may not align.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity.
Use anonymized excerpts for research.
Check internal data-handling policy before sharing files.
Keep compliance-sensitive work in Cursor only.
requires-engineering: document approved data classes for each tool.
